Figure_01_Molecular_reflection.caption: Figure 1. Exact reflection of one neutral (S)-naproxen conformer (PubChem CID 156391). A,B, Heavy-atom coordinates generated by ETKDGv3/MMFF94s; bonds are the molecular graph. The views use the same orthographic camera and physical scale. C, All degree-two persistent Laplacian eigenvalues at r=2.6 Å, s=3.2 Å. D, The six even probes paired with the first odd source, with bandwidth 2.4 Å and regularization 0.3. Z, d, H and ρ are scaled atomic number, heavy-atom degree, total hydrogen count and radial field. Reflection preserves distances and spectrum and reverses the signed readouts. This is a generated geometry control, not an assay result. Atoms: carbon graphite, nitrogen blue, oxygen muted red, sulfur ochre; hydrogen atoms are omitted.

Figure_02_Molecular_filtration.caption: Figure 2. Filtration of a fixed neutral L-alanine conformer (CID 5950). A-D, The same coordinates and camera at four Vietoris-Rips distance thresholds. Solid molecular bonds come from the chemical graph; thin proximity edges and translucent triangular faces come from the distance filtration and are not additional chemical bonds. E, Counts in the earlier complex. F, Every degree-two persistent eigenvalue at 130 displayed scales with s=r+0.6 Å; eigenvalues are unordered between scales because the chain space changes. No molecular two-cycle is inferred merely from a visible ring or overlapping triangular faces.

Figure_03_Persistent_filling.caption: Figure 3. Exact persistent filling fixture. K is the eight-face boundary of an octahedron with an isolated central vertex; L adds the cone of each face to that vertex. This is an abstract simplicial pair, not a Vietoris-Rips molecular example. A,B, The outer faces and internal cone faces. C, The 12-by-8 outside-face boundary matrix D has rank 7. Its one-dimensional kernel allows internal faces to cancel in a linear combination of all eight tetrahedra, although no single tetrahedron has boundary entirely in K. D, The persistent operator lifts the down Laplacian zero eigenvalue to 1. The up term uses an orthonormal kernel basis; its trace is 1. Deleting all tetrahedra with outside faces would incorrectly retain the unfilled two-cycle.

Figure_04_Source_propagation.caption: Figure 4. Propagation on the naproxen complex from Figure 1. A,B, Each triangular face is colored by bσ χσ or bσ uσ for the first probe and source, using one symmetric numerical color scale. These products are invariant under a change of storage orientation; the bare cochain coefficients are not being presented as invariant face colors. All faces are retained, although depth can occlude them in a static view. C, Eigenspace fractions of the squared norm of the first source and its resolved response, at τ=0.3. Numerically equal eigenvalues are grouped within relative/absolute tolerance 1e-8, giving basis-independent total weights. D, The corresponding positive source energy decreases with regularization. Filtering suppresses high eigenvalues; this standard resolvent effect is not evidence of improved biological prediction.

Figure_05_Atom_localization.caption: Figure 5. Orientation-independent atom localization at r=2.6 Å, s=3.2 Å and τ=0.3. A-D, Each atom receives one third of the sum of squared response coefficients on incident triangles, summed over the three sources, then divided by the total squared response norm. All four views use the same color normalization; thin wire shells mark annotated tetrahedral stereocentres. E, Source and response fractions for every cysteine heavy atom; * marks its stereocentre. F, Total annotated-stereocentre fraction divided by the uniform atom fraction for each displayed first conformer. Enrichment is descriptive, not attribution to a molecular mechanism or proof that the descriptor detects every stereocentre. L-cysteine has R absolute configuration at its alpha carbon; L does not universally mean S. Isoleucine has two annotated centres.

Figure_06_Conformer_comparison.caption: Figure 6. Conformer variation in the frozen 24-molecule pilot. A, Eight independently generated methionine conformers aligned on the first using translations and proper Kabsch rotations; pale bonds show the other seven conformers. This is not a dynamical trajectory. B,C, Molecule-level relative dispersion of the 18 pooled features across eight conformers, at r=2.6 Å, persistent s=3.2 Å, τ=0.3; the same-scale response uses s=r. Every feature matrix is divided by the triangle count. Dispersion is median distance from the coordinatewise median, divided by median vector norm plus 1e-12. All 24 molecules are displayed in the source-selected order. Lower values mean smaller conformer variation, not necessarily greater chemical accuracy. The persistent response improves this metric for 8/24 molecules. Its paired median difference from the source is +0.0592, with a molecule bootstrap 95% interval [-0.000003, 0.2184] from the frozen 5,000-resample analysis. The pilot therefore does not establish a general stability advantage.

Figure_07_Parameter_landscape.caption: Figure 7. Parameter sensitivity of the first generated tryptophan conformer. A,B, Frobenius norm of the 6-by-3 signed-readout matrix over 61 earlier scales and 60 positive regularization values, with later scale s=r+0.6 Å and source bandwidth 2.4 Å. The 3D surface connects evaluated grid values only to display the landscape; the true hard-filtration descriptor can jump at distance events. B displays identical values without perspective. C, The grid section nearest τ=0.3; its actual regularization is printed in the panel title. The norm is reflection-even and loses sign, although its underlying pooled components are odd. No robustness or biological performance optimum is inferred from this surface.

Figure_08_Filtration_calculus.caption: Figure 8. Filtration-event sensitivity on a generated alanine geometry. A, The first heavy atom, marked with a wire shell, is displaced along the fixed vector (0.65, -0.20, 0.25) Å multiplied by t; pale bonds show the endpoints. This is a coordinate sensitivity experiment, not molecular dynamics. B, First probe/source readout at r=2.6 Å and its uniform average over r in [2.35,2.85] Å, with s=r+0.6 Å and τ=0.3. The average is integrated exactly between distance and shifted-distance events, up to floating arithmetic. C, The analytic derivative of the average, decomposed into within-complex and moving-event-boundary terms. Ignoring the latter gives an incomplete derivative. Values at tied or endpoint events are not assigned a derivative by this routine.

Figure_S01_Full_molecular_atlas.caption: Supplementary Figure S1. Complete 24-molecule first-conformer atlas in the frozen source-selected order. Atom color shows the fraction of the total squared persistent-response norm assigned to that atom at r=2.6 Å, s=3.2 Å, τ=0.3. One shared color scale is used across all molecules. Molecular views are individually fitted for legibility, so their apparent sizes are not a physical cross-molecule size comparison. The exact coordinates, bonds, chemical identities and per-atom fractions are provided in source data. These are ETKDGv3/MMFF94s generated neutral conformers, not deposited experimental structures or physiological protonation states. No cases are omitted according to response quality.

Figure_S02_Localization_and_alignment.caption: Supplementary Figure S2. Localization and source alignment in the pilot. A, Median stereocentre enrichment across eight conformers per molecule, using all three source channels at r=2.6 Å, s=3.2 Å, τ=0.3. All 24 molecules are shown; the vertical reference is uniform atom allocation. The paired median response-minus-source difference is 0.0052 with a molecule bootstrap 95% interval [-0.1094,0.0484]; an enrichment advantage is not established. B, Response-source Frobenius cosine for configurations with a nonzero source. Empty triangle spaces have no defined cosine and are excluded from this ECDF; the exact denominator is recorded in source data. Strong alignment means the filter often preserves much of the source direction and does not itself establish added biological information.

Figure_09_Intrinsic_geometry.caption: Figure 9. Differential geometry of the molecular response, using the first source and probe at r=2.6 Å, s=3.2 Å, τ=0.3. A, Methionine with the terminal methyl-sulfur component rotated about the bridge bond joining heavy-atom indices 2 and 3 (zero based); wire shells mark the axis atoms and pale bonds show rotations of ±0.4 radians for illustration. All graph bond lengths are preserved. B, Norm of the mass-metric shape gradient after removing translation and rotation, for the four prespecified first conformers; weights are standard heavy-atom atomic weights and the unit is readout per Å per square-root atomic mass unit. C, Methionine curvature decomposes into a coordinate Hessian term and a path-acceleration term. Omitting the latter reverses its sign. D, The nonlinear part after removing the constant and linear response, within a much smaller angle window chosen to remain in one filtration chamber; the computed curve agrees with the full local quadratic expansion. A geometric torsion is not a molecular-dynamics trajectory or a claim about occupied rotamers.

Figure_10_External_ensembles.caption: Figure 10. External stereoisomer discrimination. A, The first eligible enantiomer example in the frozen parent-hash order (CHEMBL4792487), showing its first conformer and the other conformers of that isomer after proper Kabsch alignment; wire shells mark assigned tetrahedral centres. B, The two native supports in an uncentered two-axis SVD projection of their 18-component persistent readouts; this visualization retains an origin and does not enter any score. C, Equal-parent mean ES-AUC and 5,000-resample parent bootstrap 95% intervals on 512 parents and 5,514 conformers, at r=2.6 Å, s=3.2 Å, tau=0.3. Published GemNet, MACE and FMG embeddings use the identical source offset indices. D, Every parent in the source versus response comparison; overlapping points are retained. Persistent-minus-source mean ES-AUC is -0.0425, interval [-0.0523,-0.0326]. Native conformer differences can make an even distance representation discriminate stereoisomer labels; this does not establish reflection sensitivity. The cohort includes diastereomers and generated conformer sets, not binding measurements.

Figure_11_Parity_geometry.caption: Figure 11. Post-primary parity decomposition of native enantiomer ensembles. A,B, The odd Gaussian-kernel witness contrast between the same two supports as Figure 10, evaluated on the displayed two-dimensional slice through the full 18-dimensional normalized descriptor space (sigma=1). Markers in B are orthogonal projections; the full vectors define the kernel. b is the symmetric plot bound recorded in source data. C, Mean squared Gaussian MMD split into orthogonal mirror-even and mirror-odd RKHS contributions, using 465 verified tetrahedral enantiomer pairs from 337 parents; pair values are averaged within each parent before the displayed parent means. D, Parent ECDF of the odd fraction. Balancing each pair as (mu+mirror(nu))/2 and (nu+mirror(mu))/2 preserves exactly the odd contribution; even distance-histogram laws become identical under that operation. Unequal conformer counts retain one-half mixture weights. The projection identity holds to 6.7e-16. This diagnostic was added after the primary test and is not presented as a confirmatory endpoint or an equilibrium-distribution estimate.

Figure_12_Finite_support_limits.caption: Figure 12. A finite-support warning derived from an exact abstract descriptor law. The three equally weighted points are -3, 1 and 2, with Euclidean mean zero. A, Its positive-definite odd Gaussian Gram matrix at sigma=1. B, The scaled centered-covariance resolvent score tends to the explicit coefficient 1/(1^T G^-1 1). C, The covariance-null component creates a 1/lambda divergence; the positive covariance modes remain bounded. D, The odd kernel witness detects reflection asymmetry despite cancellation of the Euclidean mean. This is an abstract example, not an asserted molecular realization. The same finite-support mechanism can inflate an empirical conformer score as regularization decreases, so that score alone is not evidence of physical rigidity, statistical generalization or biological selectivity.

Figure_13_Ensemble_calculus.caption: Figure 13. Analytic calculus of a conformer probability measure. The deterministic first eligible bridge-bond example is CHEMBL5095395, with 19 parent conformers and 4 support points in the differentiated isomer law. A, Only the first conformer rotates; axis atoms have wire shells. Pale rotations of +/-0.3 rad illustrate the moving component and are not the tiny window used for derivatives. B, Exact second derivative of squared odd-mean norm over source-response regularization tau and Gaussian bandwidth sigma, with r=2.6 Å and s=3.2 Å. C, Centered differences of the analytic first derivative check the second derivative; the smallest step shows floating cancellation, not monotonic convergence. D, The actual local derivative change and its first-order curvature prediction. The maximum angle is 1.11e-06 rad, chosen from the 2.94e-5 Å filtration margin; every evaluated simplex list is checked unchanged. RMS normalization is recomputed and differentiated analytically. Full curvature is -0.0655425 rad^-2; omitting molecular path acceleration gives -0.141804 rad^-2. These are descriptor-law sensitivities, not forces or occupied-rotamer probabilities.

Figure_14_Biological_recognition.caption: Figure 14. Same-assay biological validation. A,B, ETKDGv3/MMFF94s geometries for measured stereoisomers CHEMBL2159489 and CHEMBL2159492, properly aligned; the first is colored and the next two have pale bonds for legibility. All eight conformers per isomer enter the analysis. These are generated geometries, not receptor-bound structures. The example is chosen by the greatest number of retained protein targets, breaking ties by parent hash, without selecting on affinity. C, Differences in ChEMBL pKi within the same assay, displayed separately for four human protein targets; positive values favour A. Target medians summarize multiple retained assays only after each within-assay difference has been formed. D, All 103 constitutional parents from 143 comparisons against 65 human single-protein targets. Pair/target values receive equal weight within a parent. E, Gaussian ensemble MMD versus absolute affinity difference, with 5,000 parent bootstrap replicates. The primary persistent-response association is rho=0.0499, interval [-0.1537,0.2463], and does not establish predictive value. ECFP4 uses radius two, 2,048 bits and chiral tags; the achiral fingerprint is identical within these graphs. Records require exact Ki, nM units, human single-protein targets, assay confidence nine and no retained validity/duplicate flag. Assay and activity identifiers remain in source data. The observed target mix is fixed; the interval is not evidence of generalization to unseen targets.

Figure_15_Kernel_shape_metric.caption: Figure 15. Differential geometry and the rank bottleneck of the odd kernel. A, Exact radial and tangential eigenvalues of the pullback metric of the odd Gaussian feature map. The sharp uniform lower coefficient is c0=(1-2 exp(-3/2))/2. B, A three-dimensional section of its tangent unit ball at ||z||/sigma=sqrt(3/4), sigma=1; this is feature-space geometry, not a molecular surface. C,D, The same 31-atom geometry CHEMBL5095395 with atom participation in a maximum-sensitivity direction and a computed null direction of its response Jacobian. Colors share one normalization and sum to one within each mass-normalized tangent. E, The 18 singular values in mass-orthonormal proper-rigid quotient coordinates, at r=2.6 Å, s=3.2 Å and tau=0.3, using a fixed baseline response scale for this local experiment. F, The unconstrained labelled shape space has dimension 87; numerical rank is 18 and 69 first-order directions are invisible. This saturates the dimension lower bound. The local kernel metric has the same null space, with the proved spectral sandwich. A null first derivative is not a claim of global invariance, unchanged chemistry, or zero physical force; bond-constrained conformer manifolds have a different dimension. Central differences check both displayed directions to vector errors below 6.1e-11.
